questions.question: Which OneStream data source type is described as having a standard, repeatable, and consistent format?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Fixed Files are data files with a standard, repeatable, and consistent format — fields sit at fixed positions in every row. A is incorrect — Delimited Files separate fields with a character rather than fixed positions. C is incorrect — Connectors pull data directly from an external system. D is incorrect — this type copies data between cubes or scenarios, not an external file format.

questions.question: Which OneStream data source type separates data using a special character, such as a comma or semicolon?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Delimited Files contain data separated by a special character such as a comma or semicolon. A is incorrect — Fixed Files use consistent field positions rather than a separator character. C and D are incorrect — neither describes a file format defined by a delimiter character.

questions.question: Which OneStream data source type provides the ability to import data directly from an external system, such as FX rates?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Connectors provide the ability to import data directly from an external system, with FX rates given as a specific example in the source material. A and B are incorrect — these are file-based formats, not a live connection to an external system. D is incorrect — this type moves data within OneStream (cube to cube/scenario), not from an external system.

questions.subtopic: Data Source Types — Data Management Export Sequences
questions.question: Which OneStream data source type is used to copy data from one cube or scenario to another?
questions.explanation: D is correct: Data Management Export Sequences are used to copy data from one cube or scenario to another within the application. A, B, and C are incorrect — these all bring data in from outside sources (external systems or files) rather than moving data between existing cubes or scenarios.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists the valid OneStream data source types?

options.C: Fixed, Delimited, Connectors, Data Mgmt Export Sequences

questions.explanation: C is correct: the four valid OneStream data source types are Fixed Files, Delimited Files, Connectors, and Data Management Export Sequences. A, B, and D are incorrect — none of these lists match the actual four source types; .DAT and XML are not standalone OneStream data source type categories in this context.

questions.question: What is the purpose of transformation rules in OneStream?

options.A: To tell OneStream where to read the data from
options.B: To map data from source systems to the financial model
options.C: To transform Cube View Profiles into transformation rule profiles
options.D: To transform source data into a machine-readable format

questions.explanation: B is correct: transformation rules map data coming from source systems onto the financial model (the application's dimensions and members). A is incorrect — that describes the role of a data source, not a transformation rule. C and D are incorrect — these do not describe any real transformation rule function.

questions.question: Which type of transformation rule would an administrator use to map a delimited list of source entities to a single target entity?
questions.explanation: D is correct: a List transformation rule lets you create a delimited list of source members that all map to the same target member. A is incorrect — Composite rules combine multiple source dimension values into one mapping decision, a different mechanism. B is incorrect — Mask rules use wildcard characters to match patterns, not an explicit delimited list. C is incorrect — One-To-One maps a single source member to a single target member, not a list of sources to one target.

questions.question: Which type of transformation rule explicitly maps a single source dimension member to a single target dimension member?
questions.explanation: B is correct: a One-To-One transformation rule creates an explicit, single-source-to-single-target mapping. A is incorrect — Composite rules combine multiple source values. C is incorrect — Mask rules use wildcards to match a pattern of source members rather than one explicit member. D is incorrect — List rules map several source members to one target, the reverse relationship.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the flip sign property in a transformation rule?

options.B: To convert a negative number to a positive, and vice versa
options.C: To set the visibility of dimensions
options.D: To clear data from the cube

questions.explanation: B is correct: the flip sign property reverses the sign of an incoming value — converting a negative to a positive or a positive to a negative — often needed when a source system's sign convention differs from OneStream's. A, C, and D are incorrect — none of these describe what flip sign actually does.

questions.question: What type of error occurs when data is mapped to a parent member during import?
questions.explanation: C is correct: data cannot be loaded to a parent member, so the result is an Invalid Intersection error. A is incorrect — Data Source errors occur while importing data itself (e.g., a changed file format), not because of a bad mapping target. B is incorrect — Transformation Rule errors occur when source data is validated against the mappings, a distinct stage. D is incorrect — 'Validation error' is not the specific OneStream term used for this case.

questions.question: During which phase do Invalid Intersection errors occur?

options.B: When source data is validated against the mappings
options.C: During the Validation phase when intersections in the data are invalid

questions.explanation: C is correct: Invalid Intersection errors occur during the Validation phase, when intersections present in the data are found to be invalid. A is incorrect — that describes when Data Source errors occur. B is incorrect — that describes when Transformation Rule errors occur, a separate error category. D is incorrect — certification happens well after data validation, not when this error type is generated.

questions.question: Which data load method only adds rows that were excluded from the previous file load, without changing any data already loaded for the source file?
questions.explanation: C is correct: Append adds only the rows not included in the previous load, leaving previously loaded data for that source file untouched. A and B are incorrect — both Replace variants overwrite existing data rather than preserving it. D is incorrect — 'Merge' is not a standard OneStream data load method name in this context.

questions.question: How should an administrator extract a copy of an application in OneStream?

options.A: Go to the OnePlace tab, select Load/Extract, select the Extract tab, select Application Zip File, click Extract
options.B: Go to the System tab, select Load/Extract, select the Extract tab, select Application Zip File, click Extract
options.C: Go to the Application tab, select Load/Extract, select the Extract tab, select Application Zip File, click Extract
options.D: Go to Application > Tools > Load/Extract directly

questions.explanation: B is correct: extracting an application is done from the System tab, via Load/Extract > the Extract tab > Application Zip File > Extract. A and C are incorrect — OnePlace and Application are not where this system-level extraction function lives. D is incorrect — it skips the required Extract tab and Application Zip File selection steps.

questions.question: Which two items are NOT included when an application is extracted as a zip file? (Select 2.)
questions.explanation: C and D are correct: FX Rates and Data are explicitly excluded from an application artifact extract. A and B are incorrect — Cube Views and Form Templates ARE included, as they are Application Artifacts captured by the extract.

questions.question: What primary file format is used for OneStream artifact extracts?
questions.explanation: C is correct: OneStream imports and exports application artifacts using XML format. A, B, and D are incorrect — none of these is the primary format used for artifact extracts.

questions.question: Where can an administrator select Find Modified Items within Application Load/Extract?
questions.explanation: B is correct: Find Modified Items is found within the Extract tab when extracting metadata items only. A, C, and D are incorrect — this option is specific to the Extract tab, not the Load tab, the toolbar, or the System tab generally.

questions.question: What is the Dimension Comparison Utility used for in OneStream?

options.A: To compare two dimension extracts, determining the differences between the two files
options.B: Editing, copying and pasting between two dimension extracts
options.C: To identify and load changes from one dimension extract to another
options.D: To merge two dimension extracts into one

questions.explanation: A is correct: the Dimension Comparison Utility compares two dimension extracts and determines the differences between them. B, C, and D are incorrect — these describe editing, loading, or merging actions, none of which is the utility's actual comparison-only function.

questions.question: What does a yellow row indicate within the Dimension Comparison Utility?

options.B: At least one non-immediate descendant has been changed
options.C: The member's properties, or at least one immediate child, have been changed

questions.explanation: B is correct: a yellow row means at least one non-immediate descendant (further down the hierarchy) has been changed. A is incorrect — removal is indicated by a different marker. C is incorrect — that describes a different row-color condition, tied to immediate children or direct property changes. D is incorrect — addition is also indicated by a different marker, not yellow.
